stem:
During arthroscopy of a 27-year-old athlete's injured knee, the surgeon notes that the bone ends glide smoothly within a fluid-filled space.

Friction between these bone ends is normally minimized by which of the following?

options.label: A
options.misconception: Stabilizing structures are being cast as the friction reducers.
options.explanation: Ligaments hold the bones together and resist abnormal motion, and a meniscus pads or smooths movement; neither coats the bone ends or lubricates the cavity.

options.label: B
options.text: Articular cartilage and the synovial fluid
options.misconception: None; cartilage coating plus lubricating fluid make the joint nearly frictionless.
options.explanation: A thin layer of articular cartilage covers the articulating surfaces, and synovial fluid secreted by the synovial membrane lubricates the joint cavity, so the bone ends glide without grinding.

options.label: C
options.text: The fibrous layer of the articular capsule
options.misconception: The joint's outer wall is being cast as the anti-friction element.
options.explanation: The fibrous capsule forms the walls of the joint cavity and provides strength; friction at the bone surfaces is handled by cartilage and synovial fluid.

options.label: D
options.text: Bursae interposed between skin and bone
options.misconception: Extra-articular cushions are being cast as intra-articular lubrication.
options.explanation: Bursae reduce friction OUTSIDE the joint (between skin, tendons, and bone); they do not lie between the articulating bone ends.

options.label: E
options.text: Tendons that cross the joint to insert
options.misconception: Force-transmitting structures are being cast as friction reducers.
options.explanation: Tendons transmit muscle force across the joint; they do not coat the articulating surfaces or lubricate the cavity.

context: Learning objective: synovial joint anatomy. Joint cavity (its presence defines a synovial joint) walled by the articular capsule; articulating bone surfaces covered by articular cartilage; synovial membrane secretes lubricating synovial fluid; ligaments strengthen; some joints add a meniscus.
